question: Why does retrying the same PUT leave the requested state unchanged?

scenes.caption: Same PUT twice, same stored result

narration.text: Idempotent means doing the same overwrite twice leaves the same result. I promise one repeated PUT that stores value v1 twice and still reads v1. Watch the shop sign first, then the real request trace.
The shopkeeper hangs the CLOSED sign. A visitor repeats the instruction. The keeper checks, and the same sign stays up.
The client sends PUT value v1. The service stores v1. The client retries the same PUT. The service stores v1 again, logs the repeat, and replies with the same value.

sources.supports: Section 9.2.2 defines idempotent methods and notes repeated requests have the same intended effect.
Section 9.3.4 defines PUT as replacing the state of the target resource with the enclosed representation.
